clue.text: Winner got up the game

definitions.meaning: at a shoot, the person who drives birds into the air for the guns does this

explanation.definitionFit: A victor beats the opposition, and on a shoot the person flushing out birds for the guns is called by the same name.

clue.text: No robbery where many lines are taken

definitions.text: No robbery where many lines are taken

parts.words: No robbery where many lines are taken
parts.note: the proverb 'fair ... is no robbery' joined to a telephone building where many lines are connected

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'a fair exchange is no robbery', and a telephone exchange is where many lines are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A swap is no theft, says the proverb, and the telephone switching centre handles many lines.

clue.text: Iterates bad writing

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of the word are in a faulty order and must be put right

explanation.surface: Repeating yourself makes for poor prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' tells you to rearrange ITERATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written work on a subject.

clue.text: Yet-sending back to custody does not mean forgiveness?

definitions.text: Yet-sending back to custody does not mean forgiveness?

parts.words: Yet-sending back to custody does not mean forgiveness?
parts.note: the word, split as ..., looks like sending again, yet it means a pardon or a cut in a prison term

explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE- plus MISSION it seems to mean sending back; in fact it is the reduction of a sentence or the forgiving of sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is the cancelling of a debt or penalty, or the pardoning of sins.

clue.text: It connects a master-stroke with fish

parts.note: a coup is a brilliant stroke or move
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Something links a brilliant move with a catch of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupling is a device joining two parts, such as railway wagons, together.

clue.text: Where the Welsh have vehicles for sale and poultry on loan?:

parts.note: a car mart is a market selling motor cars
hens are farmyard poultry
hire means use for a fee, on loan

explanation.surface: A Welsh town has a car showroom and a scheme for renting chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmarthenshire is a county in south-west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmarthenshire is a county in south-west Wales, home to many Welsh people.

clue.text: Cutting out-and perhaps planting ?-the border

definitions.meaning: cutting cloth with a zigzag edge, or cutting a scalloped pattern
setting pinks, the garden flowers, along a flowerbed edge

explanation.definitionFit: Pinking shears cut a zigzag edge, and a gardener edging a bed with pinks, a kind of carnation, could be said to be at work pinking it.

clue.text: Rude answer:

parts.note: the word, split as the reply '...', is the very opposite of what it says

explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M POLITE it is an answer to a question about one's manners, but as one word it means rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking good manners; discourteous.

clue.text: For tying an effigy ready for collection?"

definitions.text: For tying an effigy ready for collection?"

parts.words: For tying an effigy ready for collection?"
parts.note: a guy is the effigy of Guy Fawkes that children show while collecting pennies, and cords would tie it up

explanation.walkthrough: Before Bonfire Night (5 November) British children wheel round a stuffed effigy, a 'guy', asking for a 'penny for the guy'; ropes to tie it would be guy ropes, really tent lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes are the lines that hold a tent or mast in place.

clue.text: Mark exclamatory: bird

definitions.meaning: printers' and journalists' slang for an exclamation mark
a large South American waterbird named for its loud cry

explanation.definitionFit: Old print-room slang calls the exclamation mark by this name, and it is also a South American bird with a harsh call.

clue.text: Quick as we're told to make it-with a camera ?

definitions.text: Quick as we're told to make it-with a camera ?

parts.words: Quick as we're told to make it-with a camera ?
parts.note: 'make it quick' is said as 'make it ...', and a camera takes snaps, so the word fits both halves

explanation.walkthrough: The everyday order 'make it quick' uses this word, and the camera adds a second sense: full of snapshots.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisk or fast, as in the command to hurry up, with a nod to photographic snaps.

clue.text: Disney's classic fathead takes worker to the. Continent

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word fat
the worker ant is a crossword staple
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: A stupid person sends an employee abroad to the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fathead' looks like an insult but is read as 'head of fat', the letter F; 'takes ... to' joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Disney animated film set to classical music.

clue.text: What news on the — ?" asked Shylock

definitions.text: What news on the — ?" asked Shylock

parts.words: What news on the — ?" asked Shylock
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from The Merchant of Venice, where Shylock asks about events at the Venetian exchange

explanation.walkthrough: Shylock's line in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice names the bridge and merchants' quarter of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The bridge over the Grand Canal in Venice, home of the merchants' exchange in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Changing, position in fights perhaps:

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of these words are only one possible arrangement of them

explanation.surface: In a scrap the combatants keep moving about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange IN and FIGHTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving from one place to another is shifting.

clue.text: It may be the last word, in some lingo anyway.

definitions.text: It may be the last word, in some lingo anyway.

parts.words: It may be the last word, in some lingo anyway.
parts.note: the newest coinage is 'the last word', and it may only exist in some jargon

explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word' means the latest thing, so a freshly minted term is just that.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression.

clue.text: For his: sake we protest

parts.note: the exasperated exclamation 'for ...'s sake' names a man whose sake is invoked in protest

explanation.walkthrough: The mild oath 'For Pete's sake!' is an exclamation of protest.
explanation.definitionFit: The name used in the exasperated cry of protest 'for ...'s sake'.

clue.text: How this burglar may choose where to use this means of entry

definitions.text: How this burglar may choose where to use this means of entry

parts.words: How this burglar may choose where to use this means of entry
parts.note: to pick is to choose, and the lock is where a thief applies the tool

explanation.walkthrough: PICK means choose and LOCK is where the tool is used, so the burglar's name describes how they choose.
explanation.definitionFit: A picklock is a thief who opens locks, or the tool used to do it.

clue.text: One nervous to sound the alarm?

definitions.meaning: the vibrating hammer in an electric bell or alarm

explanation.definitionFit: A person who quakes is one, and so is the vibrating part that rings an electric bell.

clue.text: Discreet coughs at the Borders?

definitions.meaning: edges of cloth folded and stitched

explanation.definitionFit: A hem is both a little cough to attract attention and the turned-up edge of a garment.

clue.text: Astronomer, as supporter of Botticelli's Venus, we hear?

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken and sounds like the stargazer's name

parts.note: in Botticelli's painting The Birth of Venus the goddess stands on a scallop shell

explanation.surface: A stargazer is said to have backed the painter's goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' marks a homophone: 'her shell', what Venus stands on in Botticelli's painting, sounds like the astronomer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: William Herschel discovered the planet Uranus in 1781.

clue.text: Currently used for factory running?

parts.note: 'currently' means by a current of water, and the factory is a mill whose wheel it turns

explanation.walkthrough: 'Currently' looks like 'at present' but means 'by means of a current': the channel of water that drives a mill wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the fast channel of water driving a mill wheel.

clue.text: Does this-animal look before leap?

parts.note: the proverb 'look before you leap' is read with 'ante' (before) followed by 'lope' (a bounding run)

explanation.walkthrough: The animal's name splits as ANTE, Latin for before, and LOPE, a loping stride, echoing the proverb 'look before you leap'.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a fast, leaping hoofed animal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: They provide, cover for a gin cocktail in the Swan perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the mixed gin letters inside the other jumbled word
perhaps suggests the bird's name may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: Sunshades shelter drinkers enjoying a gin mix at a pub called the Swan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' turns GIN into ING and 'perhaps' turns SWAN into AWNS; 'in' puts ING inside after AWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Awnings are canvas canopies that shade windows or shopfronts.

clue.text: Wrapper for a Kipling novel? Definitely not

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel of India
the exclamation 'oh no!', written O NO, is an emphatic refusal

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a dust-jacket belongs on a Kipling book and is firmly refused.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a loose robe wrapped round the body and tied with a sash.

clue.text: Colourful material for "Who. Killed Counsel?"

parts.note: shot dead
a silk is a senior barrister, a Queen's Counsel, who wears a silk gown

explanation.surface: A whodunnit title asks which barrister was murdered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who Killed Counsel?' reads like a detective story; the answer to it is SHOT SILK. A silk is a British senior barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot silk is woven with threads of different colours so it changes hue in the light.

clue.text: Does an alumnus yearn for such a figure?

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil
to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a former student pines for something.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is a British term for a school's former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangular shape longer than it is wide.

clue.text: Pat uses his arm in trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Pat puts his arm to use when there is a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a man's name or a gentle touch; it is the stock nickname for a man from Ireland. 'trouble' tells you to rearrange HIS ARM IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat, short for Patrick, is the traditional nickname for a man from Ireland.

clue.text: Madly keen to engulf Cupid in oil

indicators.note: engulf means swallow up, so the god's name goes inside the jumbled letters
madly means wildly, so the letters of keen are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Eros is the Greek counterpart of Cupid, god of love

explanation.surface: Someone passionately wants to drown the love god in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' makes KENE from KEEN, and 'to engulf' puts EROS inside it after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin, a fuel oil.

clue.text: How to prepare wine, say, for this fish?

indicators.note: say signals the words spoken, sounding like the fish's name

parts.note: the instruction 'mull it' tells you to heat and spice the wine

explanation.surface: A cook asks how to make wine go with a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a homophone: the instruction 'mull it' sounds like the fish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The mullet is a common sea fish, grey or red.
